newsitem.title: USA: Southdown says Cemex could pay duties.
newsitem.headline: Southdown says Cemex could pay duties.

text.p: Southdown Inc said on Friday that the U.S. Department of Commerce issued the final dumping margins in two reviews regarding imported cement from Mexico's CEMEX SA, which may face dumping duties.
In the fourth review, covering the period of August 1993 to July 1994, the Commerce Department determined CEMEX's dumping margin to be 109.43 percent, said Southdown, a cement and concrete company.
In the fifth review, covering the August 1994 to July 1995 period, Commerce found a 103.82 percent dumping margin.
A Southdown spokesman said the reviews have determined that Cemex is selling the cement at a higher price in its home market than in the United States.
If these rulings are upheld on appeal, CEMEX will be required to pay antidumping duties in excess of $48 million, or over $32 per ton of cement, Southdown said.
